# Affine-base weighted projective buffers and an exact two-parity minimax

This note supplies a genuine new buffer parameter: a positive affine
function of the integer base. It retains joint concavity and the exact
projective normal cancellation. In one actual four-fiber example its
normalized minimax restores BOTH ordinary deepest witnesses, whereas
EVERY positive unweighted energy power selects only one. No general
interior attainment or OC payment follows.

Dependencies are the joint energy concavity/equality theorem, the buffered
fixed-face cover and contact continuation, and the all-source calibration
`candidate 1298c8ea2c6ec3df`.
The latter and its ordinary-depth dependency were independently audited
in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. What exact projective alignment permits

Let N=d+1, E_z(x)>0 in the interior of a positive convex fiber, and a_z(x)
its unique projective energy minimizer. The proved envelope identity is

    grad_x E_z=N E_z a_z.

Therefore a positive C1-in-fiber buffer f has

    grad_x f=f a_z                                      (1)

EVERYWHERE in that fiber if and only if

    f(z,x)=c(z) E_z(x)^(1/N),   c(z)>0.                  (2)

Indeed grad_x[log f-(1/N)log E_z]=0 on the connected convex interior.
The constant c can depend on the base. This is a characterization of
alignment throughout the fiber, not a claim about conditions imposed at
only finitely many marks.

For the unweighted power f=(E/M)^r, instead grad f=Nr f a. If its active
buffered normals satisfy sum rho u=epsilon grad f, the local projective
map sends their normals to u-epsilon f a; their sum is

    epsilon (Nr-1) f a.                                (3)

Thus varying r loses exact cancellation unless r=1/N or the selected
mark has a=0. Concavity alone does not repair (3).

## 2. A concave aligned class with a real base parameter

Let ell be a fixed positive concave function on the real base polytope B.
Define

    f_ell(z,x)=(ell(z) E_z(x)/M)^(1/N).                 (4)

It is jointly concave. Namely, put F=E^(1/d), already jointly concave.
Then

    f_ell=M^(-1/N) F^(d/N) ell^(1/N).

The weighted geometric mean is concave and coordinatewise increasing on
the positive quadrant. Its composition with the two concave functions
proves the claim. Continuity and zero own-boundary values follow from E.
Equation (1) holds exactly, since ell has no continuous-coordinate
variation. The within-fiber covariance norm Gamma can be used unchanged.

We specialize below to POSITIVE AFFINE ell. Its normalization is

    sum_(z in P) V_z ell(z)=M,  V_z=|K_z|.              (5)

This removes trivial multiplication of the buffer by a constant. If
g_bar=sum V_z z/M, every such ell is

    ell(z)=1+b.(z-g_bar),  ell>0 on B.                  (6)

In the affine span of B the open parameter domain is bounded, with compact
nonnegative closure. To see boundedness, g_bar is in relint B because all
V_z are positive; hence B-g_bar contains a relative ball. Positivity on
that ball bounds b. The boundary ell>=0 is a real possibility, not an
assertion that a useful minimizer lies in the positive domain.

The construction is covariant under lattice-preserving affine base maps
if ell is transported as a scalar base function. Common fiber linear maps
multiply E and M by the same determinant; within-fiber affine shears
preserve their quotient and transform Gamma as already proved.

A positive global source chart remains available. A full supergradient
of F at a source (p,y) gives a nonnegative tangent ratio L_F on C. The
full tangent ratio of f_ell can be chosen as

    L=(d/N)L_F+(1/N)ell(z)/ell(p)>0.                   (7)

Its continuous coefficient is exactly a_p, and its own-fiber restriction
is 1+a_p.(X-y). The uniform bound in (7) is at least
min_B ell/[N ell(p)]. For a positive concave ell use its affine tangent
in place of ell in this expression; that tangent majorizes ell.

## 3. Fixed-face equality now gives marked homotheties

Apply the abstract buffered fixed-face construction with (4), with ell
positive AFFINE and held fixed. The same weighted-contact argument forces
f_ell to equal one affine tangent at all buffered maximizing marks on the
selected minimal deepest-base face and on their interpolating segments.

Take any two such marks. Along their segment, equality must hold both in
the concavity of F and in the weighted geometric mean. The latter equality
holds precisely when the pairs (F,ell) at the two endpoints are proportional.
Consequently

    F_z/ell(z)=constant                                (8)

on the face. The joint energy equality theorem then says that the entire
marked fibers are positive homotheties, with scale ratio ell(z)/ell(w),
and all intermediate target fibers are exactly the marked Minkowski sums.
Thus there are one fixed convex body K_* and an affine marked graph y(z)
with

    K_z=y(z)+ell(z)K_*                                 (9)

on the whole real selected face. Each selected base has a unique contact
mark: two marks in the same bounded body would have to make its centered
translates equal. Convex interpolation and this uniqueness prove that
marks from different convex representations agree, yielding the affine
graph. Energies and volumes now scale as ell(z)^d; they need not be equal.

This replaces the equal-energy TRANSLATION conclusion for constant ell.
That old conclusion must not be imported into (4).

There is a safe ordinary mass consequence on this face. Its ordinary
fiber centroids are y(z)+ell(z)g_*, an affine graph. Apply the archived
weighted integer centerpoint theorem to the actual fiber volumes on its
lattice-complete base set J: some base has every containing pure-base
halfspace of weight at least M_J/k(J). At its ordinary fiber centroid,
any ambient cap contains the centroids in a corresponding closed base
halfspace. Ordinary Grunbaum in each such fiber therefore gives raw mixed
mass at least Gamma_d M_J/k(J). Outside fibers may only add mass.
This is the standard affine-centroid-graph payment with the ACTUAL masses;
it does not exhaust the total mass of a general family.

## 4. A necessary interior minimax condition for affine ell

Fix the body, epsilon, covariance, and normalization (5). Suppose a
positive affine ell is an interior local minimizer of the maximum buffered
raw depth over this parameter domain. Suppose its buffered maximizers
admit the regular selected groups in the continuation theorem. By the
same-quantile lemma their minimal deepest-base faces are singletons p_i.
Write E_i,f_i,B_i for the corresponding contact quantities and put

    delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i>0.

A feasible infinitesimal affine perturbation phi has zero volume mean,
sum V_z phi(z)=0. The body, M, and Gamma do not change. The contact-minimum
expansion is

    alpha_i'=-epsilon f_i phi(p_i)/(N ell(p_i)).

Exact quantile continuation therefore supplies the covering derivative

    q_i'=delta_i phi(p_i)/(N ell(p_i)).                (10)

If all derivatives (10) were strictly negative, the same finite cover
and the strict gaps off the old maximizing bases would give a genuine
decrease. Finite-dimensional separation thus yields eta_i>=0, sum eta=1,
with

    sum_i eta_i delta_i phi(p_i)/(N ell(p_i))=0         (11)

for every affine zero-volume-mean phi. Equivalently there are positive
nonnegative normalized weights omega_i, supported on the maximizing
bases, such that

    sum_i omega_i p_i=g_bar.                           (12)

Here omega_i is proportional to eta_i delta_i/ell(p_i). In particular
an interior parameter minimum requires g_bar in conv{p_i}.

This is a necessary condition using proved upper-cover responses. It
does not presume differentiability of the global maximum, nor require
that the cover derivative equal its exact derivative. It also does not
establish interior attainment. At ell=0 on part of B the positive-buffer
interiority, derivative, and projective chart arguments need separate
treatment. Supporting menus also require their nonlinear continuation
rather than silently substituting regular coareas.

If the body changes while ell is fixed, the usual energy/mass derivative
in (4) is unchanged. If ell is updated, it gains the additional term
f_ell dot ell/(N ell). Constraint (5) itself then differentiates with the
actual changing volumes; that normalization work must be retained.

## 5. Every positive unweighted power breaks the given exact tie

Use the actual interval family

    K0=[47/50,26/25], K1=[-11/10,1],
    K2=[-23/25,23/25], K3=[-9/100,9/100].

The fully certified ordinary depth is Q=11/10, attained exactly at
(1,0),(2,0), and M=211/50. The within-fiber covariance is
Sigma=1937167/6330000<1. At the two marks

    E1=44/21>E2=46/25.

For ANY r in (0,1], replace the aligned power by (E/M)^r. The physical
threshold shift is delta_i(y)=epsilon sqrt(Sigma)(E_i(y)/M)^r.
Because E_i<=V_i<M, delta_max<epsilon uniformly in r. On the same
|y|<=1/1000 neighborhoods from the calibration, E_i>1, |E_i'|<1, and

    |delta_i'|=epsilon sqrt(Sigma) r (E_i/M)^r |E_i'|/E_i<epsilon.

Thus the exact original all-source proof applies uniformly for
0<epsilon<=1/10000: the only candidates are the same two marks, with
values Q+delta_1(0) and Q+delta_2(0). The former is strictly larger for
EVERY r>0. Varying the positive power cannot preserve this actual tie.
For r!=1/2 it additionally loses the normal cancellation (3) at the
noncentral first mark, whose a=-1/22 is nonzero.

## 6. Exact normalized affine-base minimax restores both parities

For the SAME body, its volume base barycenter is

    g_bar=316/211.

Use f_ell from (4), d=1, and ell_b(z)=1+b(z-g_bar). The nonnegative
normalized parameter interval is exactly

    -211/317<=b<=211/316.                              (13)

Its endpoints allow ell to vanish at one extreme base. Both inner ell
values remain positive throughout (13).

The all-source calibration is UNIFORM over this entire closed interval.
Indeed (5) and ell>=0 give ell_i V_i<=M, so delta_i(y)<=epsilon sqrt(Sigma)
for all sampled sources. On the two inner neighborhoods,

    |delta_i'|
      <=epsilon sqrt(Sigma)/(2 sqrt(V_i)) * |E_i'|/sqrt(E_i)
      <epsilon/2.

All external cap statuses in the calibration remain unchanged for
0<epsilon<=1/10000. Its eta-tightened caps still exclude every point
outside the two neighborhoods, and its local Q-|y|+delta_i(y) bounds
uniquely maximize each neighborhood at zero. Hence the GLOBAL exact
buffered maximum is

    Q_epsilon(b)=Q+epsilon sqrt(Sigma/M)
       sqrt(max{E1[1+b(1-g_bar)], E2[1+b(2-g_bar)]}).    (14)

The first affine argument decreases strictly with b, the second increases
strictly. Their unique intersection is

    b_*=14137/108948,                                  (15)

strictly inside (13). It is therefore the unique GLOBAL minimizer, even
over the nonnegative completion. The four positive ell values there are

    ell0=21944/27237,  ell1=4853/5188,
    ell2=58025/54474,  ell3=130187/108948.

The common product is ell1 E1=ell2 E2=53383/27237. Thus the exact optimized
maximum is

    Q+epsilon sqrt[(Sigma/M)(53383/27237)],

attained exactly at BOTH (1,0) and (2,0), for every stated epsilon.
The two original parities are preserved. Equation (12) holds with
omega1=106/211 and omega2=105/211.

Equivalently, before normalizing the overall scale, one can take
ell(z)=1+(67/483)(z-1). Its ratio ell2/ell1=E1/E2 makes the same two
products equal. Normalizing by its volume mean gives (15).

This is an actual interior minimax example, not merely an assigned tie.
Both continuous source balances retain grad f_ell=f_ell a at every mark.
The noncentral source's response weights change consistently with its
new threshold shift; the second source remains central.

## 7. What is and is not resolved

Unweighted exponent tuning is exactly obstructed on this example.
Positive affine base weighting is a valid alignment-preserving deformation
parameter and has an exact all-source optimized success on the same body.
The general interior condition (12) is a new necessary selection constraint.

For a general body the affine equations needed to equalize several marks
may be infeasible, an optimum may lie on ell=0, and contact faces or
supporting cap branches may persist. Neither stationarity nor positivity
at an optimizer is inferred from approximation. No assertion that an
optimized affine buffer proves a mixed depth bound is made.

## 8. A genuine boundary optimum: positivity cannot be inferred

This exact counterexample and its constants were supplied independently by
Two-sided. At integer bases -1,0,1 take centered intervals of lengths

    V_-1=1/8, V_0=1, V_1=1.

Their half-length upper roof is concave and lower roof convex, so this is
an actual compatible full-dimensional body. M=17/8 and g_bar=7/17. Every
fiber is strictly lighter than M/2; every proper closed-minor occupied-
parity quota is strict.

At the middle source (0,0), any through-source nonvertical cap captures
half the own interval. Its endpoint thresholds are opposite. Since the
small centered interval A is contained in the other endpoint B, reflection
gives

    |A intersect {x>=t}|+|B intersect {x>=-t}|>=|A|=1/8.

Both continuous orientations therefore capture at least Q=1/2+1/8=5/8.
Sufficiently steep tilts capture A fully, B not at all, and half the own
fiber, giving equality. Pure-base caps are strictly larger. At a nonzero
middle mark one of the same steep orientations gives Q-|y|. At an extreme
base, steep outward tilts isolate its own ordinary interval depth, at most
1/2. Thus (0,0) is the unique ordinary deepest point, with normalized depth
5/17>1/4. This is not a bad-depth example.

The exact invariant constants are

    Sigma=1025/13056,  Sigma/M=1025/27744.

The nonnegative arithmetic-normalized affine parameters are

    ell_b(z)=1+b(z-7/17),
    -17/10<=b<=17/24.                                (16)

For 0<epsilon<=1/10000 the COMPLETE buffered maximum is

    Q_epsilon(b)=5/8+epsilon sqrt(Sigma/M) sqrt(ell_b(0)). (17)

Here is an all-source proof, including the boundary parameters. At the
middle mark the old all-normal lower bound gains exactly delta_0 in the
proper own trace; endpoint gains are nonnegative. The two steep caps
attain equality. At every other middle mark the same steep cap facing y
has mass at most Q-|y|+delta_0(y). Since E_0(y)=1-4y^2 is maximized at zero,
this is strictly below (17). Normalization and nonnegativity give
ell_i E_i(y)<=ell_i V_i<=M, so every physical shift is at most
epsilon sqrt(Sigma)<epsilon. At either outer base its own interval can
still be isolated; its buffered depth is at most 1/2+epsilon<Q. Closed
pure-base masses at the middle source remain larger than (17). Therefore
no unexamined source or tilt overtakes the stated middle value.

Because ell_b(0)=1-(7/17)b decreases strictly, (17) has its UNIQUE minimum
at the RIGHT boundary of (16):

    b=17/24,
    (ell_-1,ell_0,ell_1)=(0,17/24,17/12).              (18)

The positive affine domain has no attained minimum. Its infimum is realized
only after admitting a zero on the small endpoint fiber. All three fibers
remain positive; the failure is in positivity of the parameter, not a
vanishing physical fiber or a violated strict minor quota.

This prevents using compactness of the nonnegative parameter closure as
an automatic interior-minimum theorem. At (18) the source-zero buffer is
still positive at its own interior, but the global positive chart floor
in Section 2 disappears at the zero-ell endpoint. Any use of such boundary
parameters needs a separate argument.

## 9. Full-gradient contact continuation with changing affine weights

This section answers the exact interface question independently of any
choice of normalization for ell. Let ell_t be a differentiable path of
positive affine base functions, converging uniformly to a positive ell_0.
The bodies may follow any actual signed radial path allowed in the uniform
energy-envelope theorem. Set

    f_t(z,x)=(ell_t(z) E_(K_z(t))(x)/M_t)^(1/N).

All full-supergradient and fixed-face arguments remain valid at the old
family. The base component must include the extra term from ell:

    alpha/f=(d/N) alpha_F/F + grad ell/(N ell),
    g/f=a.                                             (19)

Here alpha_F,g_F are a full supergradient of F=E^(1/d), with its continuous
component fixed by the ordinary energy gradient. Formula (7) proves the
global positivity of this chosen tangent chart. The supporting base
resultant remains the ACTUAL

    sum_j rho_j a_base,j - epsilon alpha;

one must not replace alpha by the old unweighted energy expression.

On an old selected face, Section 3 gives (9) and unique contact marks y_z.
It also gives two useful identities:

    f_z/ell_z=constant,
    a_z=a_*/ell_z,  hence f_z a_z=constant.             (20)

Thus the common continuous resultant is consistent at every old contact,
even though the f_z, energies, and volumes are not equal. Uniqueness of
the old contact in each fiber holds independently of whether that contact
has a regular cap menu: a second tangent contact would contradict strict
fixed-fiber concavity of its positive multiple of E^(1/N).

Use the old fixed cap group, with P_i=sum rho N_ij.W, threshold h_i, old
Gamma(u_ij)=1, and finite integer contacts J_i. Define exactly

    A_i(t)=sum_j rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij),
    alpha_i(t)=min_(z in J_i, x in K_z(t))
       [P_i(z,x)-h_i-epsilon A_i(t) f_t(z,x)].          (21)

The old objective is nonnegative and has exactly the old unique contact
per base. Energy continuity and positivity of ell_0 localize new minimizers
to these finitely many marks, just as in the unweighted proof. The signed
uniform energy expansion gives

    dot f_body,z=f_z/N [dot ell_z/ell_z-C_z/E_z+D/M],   (22)

where D=-dot M and C_z is the actual old projective-kernel boundary loss
at y_z. Consequently the exact finite-contact derivative is

    alpha_i'=epsilon min_(z in J_i) f_z [
       C_z/(N E_z)-D/(N M)-dot ell_z/(N ell_z)-A_i'].   (23)

There is NO common f_i factor on a general homothetic face. The minimum
uses the same actual path and all its old contact bases. The covariance
contribution is unchanged:

    A_i'=(D-J_i^cov)/(2M).

Equation (23) follows by testing the old marks for the upper bound and
using old-objective nonnegativity at a new minimizer for the lower bound;
no differentiable contact-mark path is assumed.

Raise the weighted current quantile threshold by the exact alpha_i(t).
The weighted current buffered margins on every sampled old contact-face
fiber are nonnegative by (21), so the actual fixed-face cover persists.
Off the old deepest bases, strict gaps persist by joint upper
semicontinuity, now including uniform ell_t convergence. For regular caps
one has the same scalar response

    q_i'=-sum_j theta_ij L_ij-alpha_i'/B_i.             (24)

For positive-area supports the same alpha_i' enters the rigorously proved
nonlinear inverse equation, not a freely selected coarea formula. Thus the
weighted equality theorem supports the full contact continuation, with
(19), the unequal f_z in (23), and dot ell all retained.

This does not handle ell_0=0. The geometric-mean or arithmetic normalization
used to choose ell may create additional variation terms through dot ell;
(22)--(23) state exactly where those terms enter, without asserting their
sign or an interior minimum for either normalization.
